setting_and_object.category: Theoretical framework (with reference implementation and process-annotated testbed)

details: Existing world models (latent/representation, video-generative, 3D interactive) model only the physical substrate, so they mispredict human behavior driven by hidden beliefs, goals, intentions, emotions, and norms.

Mental World Modeling (MWM): a POMDP-style, target-centric world-modeling framework whose latent world state is factored into coupled physical and mental-social components, s_t=(s^phy,s^ment), with an explicit taxonomy of mental fields (beliefs, attention, goals, intentions, emotions, dispositions, norms, constraints, attitudes/roles, atmosphere).

Three first-class operators: rendering a target-specific first-person partial observation (including self-state and higher-order Theory-of-Mind inferences) from the third-person joint state; decomposing an action into physical carrier plus mental/semantic content; and an action-conditioned joint transition where the physical channel depends on the carrier and the mental channel on both carrier and meaning.
Accompanying insufficiency property: physical-only (or mental-only) state representations cannot match the true action distribution whenever it varies with the omitted component.

Training-free, modular, fully logged LLM/MLLM pipeline over six stages: state parsing into typed JSON, target-observation rendering (inaccessible fields set to 'Unknown'), per-option action decomposition, parallel per-branch coupled physical+mental transition, comparative branch scoring, deterministic decision.

Branch value = mental consistency, physical plausibility, social appropriateness, plus a binary safety/legality veto; batched cross-branch comparative ranking, deterministic tie-breaking outside the LLM.
Target is a 'pseudo-agent': it converts the six supplied options into branches rather than freely proposing actions.
Multimodal front-end: caption-aware image parsing; adaptive scene-change plus uniform frame sampling for video; audio track transcribed and injected alongside frames.
448 manually authored, quality-controlled situated decision records: 320 text, 100 image sequences, 28 sounding videos; 6 natural-language options each; 78% of scenes have >=2 characters.

Process-complete gold annotations: joint current state, target observation, one successor state per option (2,688 successor states), and gold action; stratified over four scene categories (interpersonal, object/resource, spatial/perceptual, risk/norm) and five everyday domains.

Shortcut controls: near-uniform gold letters, length-matched distractors, adversarial option balancing, blind options-only probes, per-item human checks (only 28 of 50 videos retained); all characters and media are fictional/synthetic.
S0 options-only floor, S1 direct answer, S2 chain-of-thought, S3 self-consistency@6, S4 free-text state, S5 typed structured state, S6 full Mentis MWM.
Ablations on S6: remove mental channel (A1), remove physical channel (A2), predict the two transitions independently (A3).
Oracle substitutions on S6: gold state (O1), gold observation (O2), verbatim option as action (O3), gold successor states (O4), plus combinations.
Channel interventions: images replaced by neutral captions; video audio removal, frame-order shuffling, audio-only.

Eight LLM/MLLM world models across two families (five OpenAI: gpt-5.6-sol, 5.5, 5.4, 5.4-mini, gpt-4.1; three Anthropic: claude-fable-5, opus-4-8, haiku-4-5); target-agent and judge roles held fixed so only the world model varies.

Metric: final-action F1 over six option letters, with paired same-record comparisons; layered structure/semantics/valuation checks via calibrated LLM judges against gold process annotations; human reference 98.5 under the identical protocol.
Single global operating point (medium reasoning effort, batched comparative-rank scoring) fixed by calibration on a frozen 30-record slice before headline runs.

key_findings.finding: Full mental world modeling is the best configuration for every model tested, and each added modeling commitment monotonically improves next-action prediction.
key_findings.evidence: Average final-action F1 rises 31.3 (options-only) to 63.3 (direct) to 74.6 (CoT) to 77.9 (SC@6) to 80.3 (free-text state) to 82.6 (structured state) to 87.9 (Mentis), with the same ordering for all eight models; the options-only floor stays flat at 29.7-33.2 across model capability.

key_findings.finding: The advantage of simulation cannot be bought with extra test-time sampling.
key_findings.evidence: Self-consistency with six sampled chains trails full MWM by 10.0 F1 on average, and Mentis with the weakest model (gpt-4.1, 84.9) exceeds SC@6 with the strongest model (gpt-5.6-sol, 83.6).

key_findings.finding: Both state channels and their coupling are individually necessary.
key_findings.evidence: Removing the mental channel costs 12.1 F1, removing the physical channel 16.5, and predicting the two transitions independently 6.4; the ordering S6 > A3 > A1 > A2 holds for all eight models.

key_findings.finding: The binding bottleneck of current MWM systems is transition simulation, not state representation or action decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: On gpt-5.6-sol, gold transitions gain +3.5 F1 (recovering 45% of the 7.8-point human gap), gold state +2.8, gold observation +1.7, verbatim actions only +0.7; all four oracles together reach 97.0 (+6.3, i.e. 81% of the gap), with gains sub-additive relative to the +8.7 sum of singles.

key_findings.finding: Gains track the type of reasoning required rather than the surface setting or input modality.
key_findings.evidence: S6-S1 gain is largest on interpersonal scenes (+26.4; S1 66.5 to S6 92.9) and smallest on object/resource scenes (+14.0), while the five domain gains are flat (19.1-22.8); the text-video gap shrinks from 6.0 (S1) to 0.3 (S6), closing already at the structured-state rung, and every media-channel intervention lowers F1 more for structured systems (S6 loses 6.4 from image-to-caption, 6.1 from audio removal, 18.8 when only audio is kept).
